summary: Model pin scope mismatch across chat/text endpoints causes silent fallback to compatibility variant
description:
Issue summary: After a staged canary rollout for redwood/open-7b-v2, some tenants using the text-generation REST endpoint observed responses served by redwood/compat-7b-quant despite an explicit model pin. Impact: Customer (TextFlow.ai) reported degraded output quality and a burst in token costs due to fallback to quantized compatibility variant. This manifests as silent transitions — the API returns 200 OK and valid payloads but content differs and latency rises.

Observed behavior:
- Tenants with explicit per-route model pin in Console maintained pins in chat endpoints but lost pins on text-generation endpoints for a subset of requests.
- Affected requests show a routing decision to compat-7b-quant at edge, but control-plane reports the route as pinned to open-7b-v2.
- Issue occurs intermittently during canary windows and correlates with prewarm rebalancing and partial edge config refresh.

Environment: production cluster in us-west, dedicated capacity for TextFlow.ai, rolling canary at 10% weight.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create tenant with explicit route pin to redwood/open-7b-v2 for text-generation REST API.
2) Start a canary promote of open-7b-v2 with 10% weight, leaving chat endpoints unchanged.
3) Generate traffic to text-generation endpoint from multiple client IPs and keep-alive streams.
4) Observe a subset of requests returning outputs consistent with compat-7b-quant while control-plane shows pins maintained.

2026-03-10T08:42:11Z control-plane[txn=tx-77] INFO pin-manager: tenant=txtflow route=/v1/generate model=open-7b-v2 state=PINNED
2026-03-10T08:43:02Z edge-proxy[req-id=def456] WARN prewarm: eviction_window_overlap for shard=sh-19
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: edge prewarm rebalance evicted prewarm tokens causing edge to resolve to fallback variant for requests arriving during the rebalance.
Traces show edge routing used local shard metadata cache which briefly lacked pin annotations during mirror-refresh following prewarm churn.
Control-plane snapshots remained correct; discrepancy appears during edge snapshot gap (TTL refresh race).
Correlated with autoscaler prewarm (warm pool rotation) at 08:42 UTC — related to change in prewarm scheduling implemented in PR 4821.
timeline_comments: 2026-03-10 09:15 - Support (Aisha): Contacted customer for request IDs and sample payloads; collected req-ids abc123, def456.
2026-03-10 10:02 - SRE (Marcus): Reproduced on staging with synthetic prewarm churn; saw edge cache misses causing route resolution to default to compatibility variant.
2026-03-10 11:20 - Eng (Lina Park): Noted that prewarm eviction logic updates shard metadata without preserving route pin flags in ephemeral snapshots (possible bug).
2026-03-11 14:45 - Support: Provided customer temporary workaround to pin at request-level header X-Redwood-Model:open-7b-v2 which bypasses edge snapshot lookup.
2026-03-12 08:10 - Eng: Deployed hotfix to edge snapshot merger to preserve pin flags during prewarm rebalances (edge PR 1872).
2026-03-13 07:30 - Support: Confirmed customer reports stability post-fix; monitoring continues.
resolution: Mitigation and fix: Applied temporary customer workaround to include explicit X-Redwood-Model header in requests to force variant selection at edge. Deployed an edge snapshot merger hotfix that preserves per-route pin annotations during prewarm/shard metadata refresh. Post-deploy monitoring for 48 hours shows no further silent fallbacks for TextFlow.ai. Next steps: add unit/integration tests covering pin annotation preservation during shard updates, add telemetry alert for pin-control-plane/edge drift, and schedule a postmortem to review prewarm rebalance behavior.
follow_up_actions: Create automated test: 'pin-preservation-on-snapshot-merge' in serving repo (owner: Lina Park).
Add an SLO alert: detect >0.1% requests with model_mismatch(control_plane,edge) in 5m window (owner: SRE).
Document request-level header workaround in Support KB and advise customers about fallback risk during canaries.
